main_body: A small farm building: a large tiled roof slope (rows 3-21) over a timber front wall with a dark door and a framed window (rows 24-35), plus a porch bench with legs below.
top_band: Roof slope, orange tiles L~147 down to ~122 at x=21, rows 3-20 (about 18 rows), under a dark outline at rows 0-2 and above a dark roof edge at row 21
evidence: At x=21 the column runs from a dark outline (rows 0-2) into a large light roof slope (rows 3-20). It then meets a darker edge line (row 21, L=69) and a dark eave shadow (rows 22-23, L=23). Below that is the wood front wall with its own shading and a dark recessed door and a window with a dark frame (rows 24-35). The roof is a clear top surface, much taller than a 1-2px rim, and it sits above a separate front face, the same way the reference houses read. The porch bench below has a visible top plank with legs under it. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The roof carries about six steps: a pale yellow highlight, light and mid orange, red, plum and a dark deep tone, with per-tile highlights that match the reference tile scallops. The wall has several wood browns with dark plank gaps and grain. The measured facts back this up: 37 colours per tile against 18 and 11 for the references, 0% flat-fill coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines are tinted brown and plum rather than black. It looks at least as rich as the references and does not read as a sticker.
